text:
maya: ran a mixed GPU run overnight to see how the kernel selector behaves under mixed seq/batch distributions. A100/H100/L40S all in the pool. posting quick notes + artifacts.

bench-bot: auto-summary: 3 kernel families exercised (flash-variant, fused-paged, paged-stream). 1200 total runs across seqlens 64/512/2048/8192 and batch sizes 1/4/16/32. logs uploaded -> https://redwood.internal/perf/bench/35321 (flamegraphs + raw csv).

maya: top-level findings:
- For short seq (<=512) flash-variant wins for latency per token on A100/H100 at bsz 1/4.
- For long seq (2048/8192) fused-paged gives better throughput on H100 at bsz >=16, but we see a surprising ~15% latency regression on A100 at seq 2048/bsz 4 where selector picked flash-variant.
- KV cache hit rates looked fine (~98%) but we saw sporadic host spill on L40S for seq 8192 at bsz 16 (mem usage ~47GB -> OOM margin).

sam: can you paste the exact bench command you ran?

maya: sure:
```
./bench_runner --model=gpt-like-7b --gpus=a100,h100,l40s \
  --kernels=flash_var,fused_paged,paged_stream \
  --seqs=64,512,2048,8192 --bsz=1,4,16,32 --reps=5 \
  --kv=true --cache_prefill=1000 --profile=flame,ptprof \
  --outdir=gs://redwood-bench/35321
```

lee: do you have the selector decision log for the regression case? which kernel was chosen and why?

maya: yes, attached in the csv (col: chosen_kernel, reason_code). For A100 seq 2048/bsz4 the selector returned `flash_var` due to heuristics that prioritize latency at bsz <=8. However PT profile shows that the attention kernel actually spent more time in host-device memcpy for KV eviction.

juan: interesting — that sounds like an interaction between our batching window heuristic and the KV eviction threshold. If the running window underestimates concurrent KV lifetime we trigger eviction mid-request. Any evidence of eviction spikes in the timeline?

maya: timeline shows 2 eviction events aligning with spikes in cudaMemcpy (see flamegraph). eviction_count column jumps from 0 to 1 during generation of token ~1200 for long sequences.

sam: can we repro locally with env vars to force the selector to pick fused_paged on A100 for that case? also try disabling adaptive_window.

maya: yep, quick experiment I ran:
```
SEL_FORCE=fused_paged ADAPTIVE_WINDOW=0 ./bench_runner --case="a100,2048,4" --reps=10
```
Results: ms/token dropped from 7.2 -> 5.9, throughput up ~18%, no memcpy spikes, eviction_count stayed 0.

lee: that strongly suggests selector heuristics mis-classified memory pressure tradeoffs for medium bsz/long seq on A100. Could be our kernel cost model assumes less KV footprint for flash_var.

juan: what's the model version for selector? last change was 0.18.2 with the 'latency_bias' tweak, rolled 2 weeks ago. Could be regression.

maya: commit in suspect window: d4a9f7a..c01b334 (selector: add latency_bias param). I can run a bisect across that range this afternoon.

sam: please also run a compact microbench that isolates just KV resident size vs seq length for the kernels. Something like:
```
for s in 512 1024 2048; do \
  ./kv_probe --gpu a100 --kernel flash_var --seq $s --bsz 4 --iters 50 >> kv_flash_var.csv; \
  ./kv_probe --gpu a100 --kernel fused_paged --seq $s --bsz 4 --iters 50 >> kv_fused.csv; \
done
```

maya: started that probe now. early numbers: flash_var KV resident ~= 3.6GB at seq2048/b4, fused_paged ~= 4.1GB (so fused uses more resident memory but avoids host copies). Strange but explains why fused avoids memcpy.

lee: so fused costs more resident memory but keeps everything on device. Our selector currently penalizes resident memory too heavily relative to memcpy cost. We should adjust cost weights to prefer device-local kernels when predicted memcpy > X ms.

sam: agreed. propose quick mitigation: increase memcpy penalty in cost model and add a fallback policy in runtime: if we detect memcpy > 1.5x baseline during first token window, switch kernel mid-stream to fused_paged where possible. Might be tricky for in-flight KV semantics though.

juan: mid-stream kernel switch risks KV address layout change. But we have safe fallback path for non-Paged streams. Need careful test. For now, a selector config tweak is safest.

maya: open a quick PR with selector weight bump and a gated flag `prefer_device_local` default false. I'll run overnight with it flagged on for A100 pool.

bench-bot: perf artifacts:
- raw csv: gs://redwood-bench/35321/raw.csv
- flamegraphs: gs://redwood-bench/35321/flame.zip
- ptprof traces: gs://redwood-bench/35321/ptprof/

sam: thanks. after your overnight, if numbers look good we can backport to production config for dedicated pools. Also let's add a regression test that replays seq2048/bsz4 on A100 with commit range anchor.

maya: will do. leaving notes in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-8276 (summary + commands + suspect commit range + quick mitigation).

lee: tiny nit — L40S spill observed: we should add a GC slack parameter for L40S pools, or reduce bsz ceiling for that machine class.

maya: noted. will include GC slack param in PR.

sam: cool. next steps: maya bisect + PR, run with prefer_device_local on A100, run regression test in CI for the case. thanks all :+1:

maya: thanks — I'll post results in this thread when bisect completes.
